subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Parallel Motion: Watt's Proudest Invention
description: A quick, practical guide to Parallel Motion: Watt's Proudest Invention.

hook.text: James Watt said his proudest creation wasn't the engine — it was a linkage.

buildup.text: Early steam pistons needed to push in a straight line, but cranks move in arcs.

discovery.text: Watt's linkage uses three bars to approximate a straight-line path.

twist.text: Peaucellier later invented a linkage that makes a perfectly straight line.

climax.text: Watt's linkage is still used in car suspensions to control axle movement.

punchline.text: Drawing a straight line with pivots took a genius.

quiz.question: What does Watt's linkage achieve?
options: It multiplies torque like a gear train
It uses pivoting bars to approximate a straight-line path
It converts rotation into reciprocating motion
